title: Solidarity delegation reception at Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri’s home in Qanawat
location: Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri’s home, Qanawat, Suwayda Governorate
scope: Local residence reception; visiting delegations reportedly came from several Syrian Druze-majority communities
organizer: Local dignitaries and families; Enab Baladi says the Al-Zain al-Din family invited local figures
participants_original: Solidarity delegations; one later report says many families visited; no number stated
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Sources report delegations and many families but no count, and do not resolve whether the private-home reception was a public forum.

title.summary: Syria Direct identifies a Jan 26 solidarity reception at al-Hijri’s home; Enab Baladi reports a Jan 26 meeting in Qanawat.

start_date.summary: Syria Direct’s photo caption explicitly dates the home reception to Jan 26; Enab Baladi also dates the solidarity meeting to Jan 26.

end_date.summary: No source records a physical departure or dissolution; the later statement urging calm is not an endpoint.

location.summary: Sources locate the reception at al-Hijri’s home in Qanawat; Al-Araby reports the arrivals at that home.

scope.summary: Photo caption and follow-up name delegations/families from several communities; no coordinated national campaign is established.

organizer.summary: Enab Baladi attributes the invitation to the Al-Zain al-Din family; no formal protest organization is identified.

demands.summary: North Press attributes an apology demand to gatherings arriving in Qanawat, but does not date that demand to the Jan 26 reception; Syria Direct describes apology demands across the broader episode. Coding this category for E001 is tentative and limited to the official-insult grievance; release was the Sheikh’s earlier request, not independently documented as a demand by reception attendees.

participants_original.summary: Sources describe solidarity delegations and many families, with no numerical estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound can be derived.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative descriptions do not establish 50 participants, and the private-home venue leaves the public-forum criterion unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: No occurrence-specific evidence establishes protester violence at the Jan 26 reception; broader episode reports of later torn portraits are not transferred.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Al-Araby’s Jan 28 local-source account says people arrived at the Qanawat home two days earlier (Jan 26), prompting Damascus intervention followed by release of the previously detained man and an apology from Luay al-Ali. This reported event-link supports accommodation, but remains attributed to local sources.

state_response.arrests.summary: Unknown. The same report says the young man had already been detained in Homs before the gathering; that prior detention is not coded as an arrest at the protest.

state_response.beatings.summary: No source reports a state beating at this occurrence.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No source reports an attempt to disperse this reception.

state_response.ignore.summary: No source establishes explicit state inaction or refusal.

state_response.killings.summary: No source reports a state killing at this occurrence.

state_response.shootings.summary: No source reports state gunfire at this occurrence.

eligibility.summary: Candidate remains pending_evidence because attendance threshold and the public character of a private-home reception are unresolved.

coding_status.summary: Researcher candidate only; no independent review.

episode_key.summary: Tentatively linked to Jan 27 Suwayda street gatherings over the same officer’s insult; shared key does not merge the reception and street events.

open_questions.summary: Resolve whether this private-home reception was a qualifying public assembly of at least 50, whether the general apology demand belongs to this exact gathering, how the reported apology/release relate to Jan 27, and when the gathering physically ended.

notes: Keep separate from the Jan 27 Suwayda city/roundabout gatherings. The Sheikh’s private home reception is not itself a state reception. Al-Araby attributes the Jan 26 arrival, Damascus intervention, release, and apology link to local sources; the youth’s Homs arrest happened earlier and is not an event arrest. No physical endpoint is established.
open_questions: Was the private-home reception a public forum for coding purposes?
Did it include at least 50 people?
Does the Jan 27 article’s general apology-demand account refer to this Jan 26 reception or a later gathering?
Can the locally attributed apology and release be independently tied to this occurrence?
When did attendees physically depart or the reception dissolve?

title: Suwayda city gatherings after security chief’s insult of Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri
location: Suwayda city streets and squares, including Samar Roundabout; Qanawat is separately reported as the site of the Sheikh’s reception and official visit
scope: Local city gatherings; the scale of coordination with visiting delegations is unclear
organizer: Unidentified local residents and supporters; no formal organizer identified
participants_original: North Press reports several gatherings; 7al calls the city gatherings limited; the SOHR-hosted Asharq account describes large crowds
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Accounts range qualitatively from limited gatherings to large crowds; none gives a count or a clear hundreds/thousands description.

title.summary: North Press and 7al report gatherings in Suwayda following the insult; the SOHR-hosted Asharq account describes the related public response.

start_date.summary: North Press published its gathering report on Jan 27 after an insult it dates to Tuesday; 7al’s Jan 28 report says city gatherings and the official visit occurred Wednesday Jan 27.

start_precision.summary: The date is day-precise from the contemporary reports.

end_date.summary: No physical departure or dissolution is reported.

location.summary: North Press’s caption locates arrivals at Samar Roundabout and the body mentions city streets/squares. 7al separately places the Jan 27 official visit at al-Hijri’s headquarters in Qanawat.

scope.summary: Reports describe city gatherings and arrivals from other Druze-majority areas; organization or a single coordinated event across sites is not verified.

organizer.summary: Local young men, residents, and supporters are described; no formal organizer is named.

demands.summary: North Press attributes a demand for the Syrian government to secure a personal apology; 7al also reports demands for transfer of military-security chief Luay al-Ali. These are coded as a political-process grievance, not as a demand about unrelated earlier detention.

participants_original.summary: Reports use qualitative and nonmatching terms: several gatherings, limited gatherings, and large crowds.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound can be derived.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative descriptions conflict and no numerical estimate or explicit hundreds/thousands benchmark is reported; the >=50 threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: North Press reports torn/destroyed Assad portraits and 7al reports protesters tearing portraits; this is coded yes under the protocol’s property-destruction example, while threats attributed to an armed faction are not counted as protester violence.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Unknown. 7al reports that the governor, Baath branch secretary, and police commander arrived at al-Hijri’s headquarters on Jan 27 to attempt to calm tensions, but the report does not establish an actual audience, negotiation, or concession and says the effort produced no result. The official visit is separate from the Jan 26 solidarity reception.

state_response.arrests.summary: Unknown. Sources describe the youth’s Homs detention before the protest trigger; this is not an arrest during or in response to the Jan 27 gatherings.

state_response.beatings.summary: No occurrence-specific state beating is reported.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No occurrence-specific state attempt to disperse is reported.

state_response.ignore.summary: No explicit state refusal or avoidance is established.

state_response.killings.summary: No occurrence-specific state killing is reported.

state_response.shootings.summary: No occurrence-specific state gunfire is reported.

eligibility.summary: Pending threshold because sources do not resolve whether at least 50 people attended.

coding_status.summary: Researcher candidate only; no independent review.

episode_key.summary: Tentatively linked to the Jan 26 Qanawat solidarity reception over the same insult; retained as a distinct city gathering because date/site boundaries and coordination are unclear.

open_questions.summary: Resolve threshold, exact locations, relation to Jan 26 reception, whether the official visit involved an actual meeting, and physical endpoint. The later apology and prior detainee release must stay attributed to the reported Jan 26 arrival unless new evidence ties them to this event.

notes: Distinct from the Jan 26 Qanawat delegation reception. North Press and local reports place street/roundabout gatherings in Suwayda; sources vary qualitatively on scale. The Jan 27 governor/party/police delegation visit to al-Hijri’s headquarters is reported as an attempted de-escalation with no reported result; accommodation remains unknown because an actual meeting or concession is not established. The apology and release reported by Al-Araby are tied to the Jan 26 arrival, not transferred to this event. No previous Homs detention is treated as a protest arrest.
open_questions: Did attendance reach 50?
Were the city streets/squares and Samar Roundabout one gathering or multiple linked sites?
Did the Jan 27 official delegation actually meet the Sheikh or protest representatives?
When did the gatherings physically end?

title: Pro-regime supporters protest against SDF/AANES in Hasakah and Qamishli
location: Hasakah and Qamishli; exact assembly sites unreported
scope: Two reported city gatherings; coordination between them is unknown
organizer: Pro-regime supporters; no organizer for the Jan 27 gatherings is identified
participants_original: Pro-regime supporters went out in protest against the SDF and AANES in both cities; no number stated
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The report describes demonstrations in two cities but provides no crowd size at either site.

title.summary: North Press distinguishes the preceding Wednesday’s demonstrations in both cities from the Jan 31 march attempt and combat.

start_date.summary: The Jan 31 report dates the occurrence as “last Wednesday,” which is Jan 27.

start_precision.summary: The relative weekday in the dated Jan 31 article supports Jan 27.

end_date.summary: The report says Asayish intervention cut the demonstrations short but does not document the physical dissolution time or an endpoint.

location.summary: The source names Hasakah and Qamishli but not specific assembly sites.

scope.summary: Two local-city demonstrations are reported; the source does not establish shared organization.

organizer.summary: The participants are described as pro-regime supporters; no organizer for the Jan 27 action is named.

demands.summary: The report characterizes the protests as against SDF/AANES; the particular policy at the Jan 27 events is not specified as clearly as the later siege-related call.

participants_original.summary: Pro-regime supporters are said to have protested in both cities; no numerical estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound can be derived.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No turnout estimate for either city; threshold cannot be inferred from the plural or from two cities.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not describe violence by Jan 27 demonstrators; later armed clashes are separate.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No accommodation by the Syrian government is documented.

state_response.beatings.summary: No protest-specific state beatings are established.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: North Press says Asayish intervention cut the demonstrations short; Asayish is the AANES de facto internal-security force. Its classification as a Syrian state response is unresolved, so the state-response field remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: No explicit Syrian-state refusal or avoidance is established.

state_response.killings.summary: No protest-linked state killing is established.

state_response.shootings.summary: No protest-linked state shooting is established.

eligibility.summary: Pending state target. The described opposition is directed at SDF/AANES, a de facto local authority; domestic-state treatment requires protocol calibration. Attendance threshold is also unresolved.

coding_status.summary: Researcher candidate only; no independent review.

episode_key.summary: Tentatively connected to the later Jan 31 march attempt over the Hasakah/Qamishli siege; separate gathering date retained, no automatic merge.

open_questions.summary: Resolve crowd sizes, site-level boundaries, exact demands, domestic-state status of the target, the nature of Asayish intervention, and physical end. Feb 2 end-of-siege reporting does not establish demonstration continuity or endpoint.

notes: North Press identifies this as the preceding Wednesday’s demonstrations in Hasakah and Qamishli, distinct from the Jan 31 attempted march and Asayish–National Defense firefight. SDF/AANES and Asayish operated as de facto authorities in a fragmented-control setting; a demand directed at them is not automatically coded as a demand on Syria’s own state. Asayish reportedly cut the gatherings short, but that action is not coded as a Syrian-state response pending actor calibration. Do not transfer combat injuries/deaths to the demonstrations.
open_questions: Did either city gathering reach 50 participants?
Were these coordinated demonstrations or distinct local actions?
What specific demand was made at each site?
Does the project treat AANES/SDF policy as a domestic-state target for these areas?
Did Asayish physically disperse attendees, and can its action be coded as a state response?
When did each gathering end?

title: Pro-regime supporters’ attempted march toward an Asayish checkpoint in Hasakah
location: Hasakah near the security complex and an Asayish checkpoint; exact route and assembly point are unreported
scope: Local attempted march; the planned government call also named Qamishli, but attendance there is not verified for this occurrence
organizer: Pro-regime demonstrators; the governor and other Syrian-government officials reportedly called for a Jan 31 demonstration on Jan 30
participants_original: Pro-regime demonstrators attempted to march toward an Asayish checkpoint; no number reported
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. An attempted march is reported but its assembly point, attendance, and participant count are not provided.

title.summary: North Press reports that pro-regime demonstrators attempted to march toward an Asayish checkpoint before an armed firefight.

start_date.summary: The North Press report describes the Sunday Jan 31 occurrence; SOHR on Jan 30 reports officials’ call for a demonstration the following day.

start_precision.summary: Both sources support a day-level Jan 31 date for the planned and reported action.

end_date.summary: No physical ending or dissolution of the attempted march is reported.

location.summary: The source locates the firefight near Hasakah’s security complex and says the march was toward an Asayish checkpoint; the precise route and assembly point are not stated.

scope.summary: The observed attempted march is reported in Hasakah. Officials’ call named both Hasakah and Qamishli, but that call does not prove a second gathering.

organizer.summary: The article attributes the call to the regime governor and other government officials; the march participants’ organizer is not identified.

demands.summary: The officials called for demonstrations against what they called the Asayish/AANES siege policy; the target is a de facto authority, not automatically the own-state government.

participants_original.summary: The source reports demonstrators attempting to march but gives no count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound can be derived.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither attendance nor a count is reported; the attempted march does not establish the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The article reports a firefight between Asayish and National Defense forces after the march attempt; it does not attribute violence to the demonstrators.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No accommodation by the Syrian government toward this attempted march is reported.

state_response.arrests.summary: No protest-specific arrests are established; arrests between armed groups in the broader tension are not coded here.

state_response.beatings.summary: No protest-specific state beating is reported.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: An armed clash followed the attempted march, but the source does not establish that it was an Asayish dispersal action against marchers; Asayish’s de facto status also remains a coding issue.

state_response.ignore.summary: No explicit state refusal or avoidance is established.

state_response.killings.summary: The article reports one Syrian-regime-affiliated fighter killed in the separate firefight; this is combat, not a protest-response killing.

state_response.shootings.summary: The reported firefight is between armed forces and is not evidence of state shooting at demonstrators.

eligibility.summary: Pending state target because the stated protest object is the AANES/Asayish siege policy; attendance and threshold are also unverified.

coding_status.summary: Researcher candidate only; no independent review.

episode_key.summary: Tentatively connected to the Jan 27 Hasakah/Qamishli demonstrations against the same siege; a separate Jan 31 attempted march is retained without merging.

open_questions.summary: Resolve attendance/threshold, whether a gathering assembled before the march attempt, precise demand and intended target, actions during the armed clash, and endpoint. Feb 2 siege resolution is not a protest end date.

notes: Keep the reported attempted march separate from the ensuing Asayish–National Defense firefight. The armed deaths/injuries belong to that combat report, not the protest or state-response fields. Officials’ call for a rally against AANES does not establish that Syrian civilians’ demand targeted the Syrian state; Asayish/AANES status is unresolved. The February 2 lifting of the siege is contextual follow-up, not a physical protest endpoint.
open_questions: Did 50 or more people assemble?
Was there a public assembly, or only an attempt to march from an unreported site?
Was the demand directed at the Syrian government, AANES, or both?
What state-response action, if any, was directed at demonstrators?
When did the attempted march physically end?
